does.text: Runs every tick over the walls. (1) Two queries (contents not resolved) have every matching entity destroyed each tick, which is the pattern of clearing one-frame request entities. (2) A wall entity that has CreateComponent but no AnimationComponent yet gets an esv::itemwall::AnimationComponent added, but only when the concentration-cleared lookup (FUN_181140a80) does not find the wall: its timer plus the wall template's ItemAnimation steps (fetched through the helper from the ItemWall template named in CreateComponent via GetItemAnimations over the ItemSpawn array). (3) If a helper call (vtable slot +0x28, labelled GetSurface by the author; that it tests a non-zero surface type is not read) returns true, a new entity is created carrying esv::itemwall::CreateSurfaceCapsuleOneFrameComponent, filled from the wall's CreateComponent plus the spell's surface radius, lifetime and status, for the surface manager to lay a surface.

does.text: Each tick the animation timer of every wall that has both CreateComponent and AnimationComponent advances by the frame's delta time. If the animation step list is empty, or a wall's key is found in the set built from esv::concentration::OnConcentrationClearedEventOneFrameComponent (helper FUN_181140a80), the wall entity is destroyed. Otherwise the steps whose time has passed are popped one by one. For each popped step, every ItemSpawn of the wall whose id equals the step's id causes a fresh entity with esv::itemwall::RequestSummonOneFrameComponent (the item spawn: name, position, rotation, spell id, wall lifetime from the helper and status), which is what asks the summon system to spawn one wall segment item. Also, for entities listed in the wall's creation result whose step mask matches the popped step, an esv::itemwall::ForcePushRequestOneFrameComponent (the wall's source plus spell id plus a vector copied from the list) is added to that existing entity if it is alive.
